title: Earth Movement
learning_objectives: Understand that the Earth is spherical.
Identify the two types of movements of the Earth.
Learn about different seasons caused by revolution.
Define solstices and equinoxes and when they occur.

production_scope.description: Opening through Word Bank inclusive; nothing after Word Bank.

section_defaults.animation_action: Advance topic-matched moving footage at the spoken cue; show the exact textbook lines in the compact teaching panel without covering the subtitle lane.

sections.title: Lesson 2: Earth Movement
sections.description: Open immediately on a child-friendly 3D Earth turning in a bright classroom-to-space setting; show only Social Studies, Class 5 and the exact lesson title in the approved title-card layout.

sections.title: Learning Objectives
sections.description: Keep the moving Earth visible behind a compact source-faithful objectives box; reveal each of the six original objectives as it is read.

sections.title: Start-Up Activity
sections.description: Show one child spinning one ball on a table, then transform the ball into a rotating Earth in space; no duplicate ball or irrelevant action.

sections.title: Who proved that the earth is spherical?
sections.description: Use the original spherical Earth figure plus distinct animated beats of a ship disappearing over the horizon, curved Earth shadow at lunar eclipse, and a circumnavigation route; labels remain authored, not AI-generated.

sections.title: The Two Movements of the Earth
sections.description: Contrast a spinning 3D Earth with the same Earth travelling around a Sun, with the two textbook terms shown side by side in the cream teaching box.

sections.title: Rotation
sections.description: Animate west-to-east Earth spin and the advancing day-night boundary; insert the exact textbook axial-tilt figure with legible original equator, axis and 23.45-degree diagram labels while the body text's 23.5-degree value is read.

sections.title: Do You Know?
sections.description: Keep rotating 3D Earth motion behind the original highlighted fact box; emphasize 1,670 kilometres per hour without fabricated speed graphics.

sections.title: Revolution
sections.description: Show a continuous 3D tilted Earth orbit around the Sun with changing daylight; use the exact rotation-versus-revolution textbook figure and distinct summer, winter, spring and autumn visual beats when each season is spoken.

sections.title: Let's Learn More
sections.description: Use one moving Earth and a precise animated clock to compare textbook 23 hours 56 minutes with the rounded 24-hour day; preserve the yellow textbook callout treatment.

sections.title: What is Solstice and When Does It Occur?
sections.description: Show the tilted Earth and Sun at December and June positions; keep December 22, June 21, Tropic of Capricorn and Tropic of Cancer as precise authored labels synchronized to the narration.

sections.title: Let's Learn More
sections.description: Use a child-friendly short bicycle stopping demonstration and then return to steady Earth rotation; maintain the original blue fact-box wording.

sections.title: What is Equinox and When Does It Occur?
sections.description: Show equal illuminated and dark Earth halves, then the complete original four-position solstice/equinox source diagram; keep all four date captions readable and correctly placed.

sections.title: Recall
sections.description: Deliberately stable cream reading card with the complete original Recall paragraph; subtle Earth motion behind it, word-highlight subtitles synchronized to reading.

sections.title: Let's Remember
sections.description: One stable, paginated teaching card presenting all five original summary lines in order, with an active line highlight and the relevant rotating globe/orbit visual in the free area.

sections.title: Word Bank
sections.description: A structured five-row original glossary card: Rotation, Revolution, Orbit, Solstice and Equinox, each exact textbook definition read with synchronized active-row and word highlights; end immediately after the last definition.
